tasks.prompt: Order the weekly jar test program used to hold coagulation on target.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional surface water plant in western Canada running a standing weekly jar test program on a prairie river source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: Monday raw water collection through the dose decision posted for the week.

cards.label: Collect a fresh raw water sample at the intake and measure turbidity, pH, alkalinity, temperature, and colour
Fill six jars with equal measured volumes and set the dose ladder around the current plant dose
Dose each jar during rapid mix, then run the standard flocculation and settling times
Measure settled turbidity, pH, and colour in every jar and record floc size and settling character
Select the lowest dose that meets the settled water targets and confirm alkalinity remains adequate
Post the selected dose for the week, file the bench sheet, and flag any dose change to the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: The weekly program samples first, tests a dose ladder under fixed bench conditions, and only then posts a dose, so plant changes rest on measured settled quality rather than habit.

tasks.prompt: Order the jar test response when raw water quality shifts mid week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan treating river water whose turbidity and colour rose after overnight rain.
tasks.configuration: Scope: detecting the raw water shift through a confirmed plant dose change.

cards.label: Confirm the shift with a fresh grab sample and compare turbidity, colour, and alkalinity with the weekly bench sheet
Collect a new raw water sample and run an unscheduled jar test series at the current conditions
Include the current plant dose as one jar so the new results can be compared directly
Choose the dose that restores settled turbidity and colour targets with adequate residual alkalinity
Change the plant coagulant feed in one step to the jar test dose and note the time of the change
Check settled water after one clarifier detention time and confirm the dose before logging the event

tasks.explanation: A raw water shift voids the old bench sheet, so a fresh jar test that includes the current dose as a reference is run before the plant feed is changed and then verified in settled water.

tasks.prompt: Order a coagulant dose optimization trial run over one production day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 operator in western Canada running a structured dose trial to reduce chemical use without losing settled quality.
tasks.configuration: Scope: trial planning through the adopted operating dose.

cards.label: Set the trial settled water turbidity, pH, and alkalinity limits and the step size between trial doses
Record baseline settled quality and sludge production at the current dose for a full detention cycle
Lower the dose by one step and hold it for at least one full clarifier detention time
Measure settled turbidity and pH and observe floc and blanket behaviour at the trial dose
Repeat the step down until settled quality approaches the trial limit, then return to the last passing dose
Adopt the last passing dose, update the dose control chart, and record trial results for review

tasks.explanation: An optimization trial moves in single held steps with a full detention time at each dose, so each settled result belongs to one dose and the adopted dose is the last one proven to pass.

tasks.prompt: Order the alkalinity supplementation program for a low alkalinity source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba on a low alkalinity source where coagulation regularly consumes most of the available alkalinity.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw alkalinity assessment through a stable supplemented coagulation program.

cards.label: Measure raw water alkalinity, pH, and turbidity across a representative week and record the pattern
Run jar tests with graded alkalinity supplement doses to find the dose that holds post coagulation pH and alkalinity on target
Set the supplement feed point ahead of the coagulant so the water is conditioned before coagulation
Start the supplement feed at the jar test dose and confirm delivery by calibration drawdown
Track treated pH and residual alkalinity daily and trim the supplement dose against the control limits
Review supplement use and treated quality monthly and update the program dose table by season

tasks.explanation: Supplementation is set by jar testing first, fed ahead of the coagulant, proven by drawdown, and then managed by daily residual alkalinity rather than by a fixed guess.

tasks.prompt: Order a coagulation pH optimization study for a coloured prairie source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Alberta treating a high colour, high organic prairie reservoir source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bench study design through the plant pH set point decision.

cards.label: Collect raw water and measure colour, turbidity, alkalinity, and natural pH
Run jar test sets at several controlled pH values using the same coagulant dose in each set
Measure settled colour, turbidity, and residual alkalinity for every pH set
Identify the pH range that gives the best colour and turbidity removal without exhausting alkalinity
Trial the selected pH set point at plant scale for a full production day and monitor settled quality
Set the operating pH band, record the acid or alkali feed arrangement, and file the study results

tasks.explanation: The study holds dose constant while pH varies, so the best pH range is proven on the bench before a plant trial fixes the operating band.

tasks.prompt: Order the polymer aid selection trial for a conventional plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional conventional plant in western Canada comparing two polymer aids to strengthen weak floc.
tasks.configuration: Scope: candidate product screening through the adopted aid and dose.

cards.label: Define the trial success measures: floc size, settled turbidity, filter run length, and aid cost per treated volume
Run jar tests with each candidate aid at graded doses on the same raw water and coagulant dose
Rank the aids by settled quality and floc strength and eliminate any aid that harms settled pH or alkalinity
Trial the leading aid at plant scale at the bench dose and watch clarifier and filter performance for a full day
Confirm the aid feed system delivers the trial dose steadily by drawdown and observation
Adopt the proven aid and dose, record the product and dose in the chemical program, and set a review date

tasks.explanation: Aid selection compares products on identical bench water first, proves the leader at plant scale, and only then writes the product into the chemical program.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal coagulant changeover from alum to a polyaluminum product.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia switching coagulant for the cold water season under its chemical program.
tasks.configuration: Scope: changeover planning through the new product in stable service.

cards.label: Run jar tests on current raw water with both products and set the starting dose for the new product
Confirm the new product storage, feed pump compatibility, and calibration for its different strength and density
Draw the old product day tank down to the planned changeover level without running the feed dry
Switch suction to the new product, prime the feed, and confirm delivery by calibration drawdown
Start at the jar test dose and monitor settled turbidity, pH, and alkalinity closely for the first detention cycles
Update the chemical log, dose tables, and safety data sheet file and brief all shifts on the change

tasks.explanation: A product changeover is dosed from fresh jar tests, not converted by rule of thumb, and feed delivery, settled quality, and records are all proven before the change is treated as complete.

tasks.prompt: Order an enhanced coagulation program to improve organics removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada increasing organics removal to limit disinfection byproduct formation, following the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw organics assessment through a sustained enhanced coagulation operation.

cards.label: Measure raw water colour, ultraviolet absorbance or total organic carbon, alkalinity, and turbidity to set the removal goal
Run jar tests at increased coagulant doses and adjusted pH to find the dose that meets the organics target
Check that alkalinity supplementation holds treated pH and residual alkalinity within limits at the higher dose
Raise the plant dose in steps, holding each step for a detention cycle while settled organics and turbidity are measured
Confirm filter performance and sludge handling can sustain the higher solids load from the new dose
Set the enhanced dose as the seasonal operating point and trend treated organics and byproduct samples on the program schedule

tasks.explanation: Enhanced coagulation raises dose for organics, not just turbidity, so alkalinity support, filter load, and sludge capacity are all proven before the higher dose becomes the operating point.

tasks.prompt: Order the settled water feedback routine that trims coagulant dose day to day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Alberta using settled water results as the daily control signal for coagulant dose.
tasks.configuration: Scope: morning settled sampling through the logged dose decision.

cards.label: Collect settled water at the clarifier effluent at the set morning time and measure turbidity, pH, and colour
Compare the results with the plant control band and with the previous three days on the trend chart
Check raw water turbidity and alkalinity to decide whether a settled change is a raw change or a dose problem
Trim the coagulant dose by the program step size only when settled results are outside the band
Recheck settled water after one detention time to confirm the trim moved quality toward the target
Plot the results and the dose on the control chart and note the decision in the process log

tasks.explanation: Daily trimming follows a fixed signal order: settled quality first, raw water context second, one small step at a time, and a recheck after a detention time before the day is closed.

tasks.prompt: Order the coagulant dose control chart review at month end.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in western Canada reviewing a month of coagulant dose and settled quality data.
tasks.configuration: Scope: data gathering through corrective actions assigned.

cards.label: Gather the month of dose, raw turbidity, alkalinity, and settled turbidity records and check for missing days
Plot dose against raw turbidity and mark periods where settled quality left the control band
Separate excursions caused by raw water events from excursions at steady raw quality
Check feed calibration records for any period where recorded dose and delivered dose may have differed
Assign corrective actions such as recalibration, jar test refresh, or dose table revision with owners and dates
File the review, update the dose table if directed, and brief the operating team on the findings

tasks.explanation: A month end review separates raw water effects from delivery effects before assigning actions, so dose table changes are not made for what was actually a calibration problem.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal winterization sequence for a small seasonal treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional seasonal plant in a Manitoba recreation community closing for the winter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: last production day through the plant secured for winter.

cards.label: Produce and store the final treated water supply and notify the community of the seasonal closure
Use or return remaining chemicals as the chemical program directs and secure what stays on site
Drain process units, filters, and exposed piping in the order that protects media and equipment
Blow out or drain small lines, sample lines, and pump casings that trap water
Set building heat to the winter holding level and confirm low temperature alarms notify the responsible operator
Lock and secure the plant, complete the winterization record, and set the spring start up inspection list

tasks.explanation: Winterization drains in an equipment protecting order, secures chemicals, and leaves heat and alarms guarding the building, with the spring inspection list written while the plant condition is known.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up sequence for a lime soda ash softening plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional lime soda ash softening plant in Manitoba starting production after a weekend shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant at rest through stable softened water to the filters.

cards.label: Review raw hardness, alkalinity, and temperature and set the lime and soda ash doses from the current dose table
Inspect lime slaker, soda ash feeder, and solids contact clarifier and confirm each is ready for service
Start raw water flow to the solids contact clarifier at a reduced rate
Start lime feed, then soda ash feed, and confirm each delivery by feeder calibration checks
Allow the sludge blanket to form and check softened hardness, pH, and alkalinity at the clarifier effluent
Raise flow to the normal rate once softened quality is on target and record doses and results

tasks.explanation: Softening start up sets chemistry from raw hardness first, proves each feeder, builds the blanket at low flow, and only raises flow once softened hardness and pH are on target.

tasks.prompt: Order the bench determination of lime dose for a hardness change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory bench program in Saskatchewan after raw hardness rose with a new well blend.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw sample analysis through the revised plant lime dose.

cards.label: Analyse the raw sample for total hardness, calcium, magnesium, alkalinity, and pH
Prepare a graded series of lime doses in bench reactors using the new raw water
Mix, react, and settle each reactor for the standard bench reaction time
Measure softened hardness, pH, and alkalinity in each reactor and note sludge character
Select the lowest lime dose that meets the softened hardness target with stable pH
Set the plant lime dose from the bench result and confirm with clarifier effluent hardness within one shift

tasks.explanation: The bench series isolates lime dose on the actual new water, and the plant dose is only adopted after clarifier effluent hardness confirms the bench choice.

tasks.prompt: Order the excess lime treatment sequence for high magnesium water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening plant in western Canada treating high magnesium groundwater by excess lime treatment.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw water entering treatment through recarbonated softened water.

cards.label: Measure raw calcium, magnesium, alkalinity, and pH and calculate the excess lime requirement from the plant factors
Feed lime to raise the reaction pH into the magnesium removal range in the solids contact unit
Hold the high pH reaction through the contact and settling zones so magnesium precipitates with the sludge
Withdraw softening sludge at the rate that holds the blanket in its target band
Recarbonate the settled water in stages to lower pH and stabilize the water before filtration
Filter the stabilized water and confirm final hardness, pH, and alkalinity meet plant targets

tasks.explanation: Excess lime treatment needs high pH contact first for magnesium removal, then staged recarbonation to restabilize the water, and filtration only after stability is restored.

tasks.prompt: Order the recarbonation sequence after lime softening.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening plant in Alberta using carbon dioxide recarbonation after a solids contact clarifier.
tasks.configuration: Scope: high pH clarifier effluent through stabilized water entering the filters.

cards.label: Measure clarifier effluent pH, alkalinity, and hardness and confirm the water needs recarbonation
Start carbon dioxide feed at a low rate into the recarbonation basin
Mix and hold the water for the basin contact time while pH falls gradually
Measure pH at the basin outlet and trim the gas feed to reach the first stage target
Pass the water through the second stage contact and confirm final pH and alkalinity are in the stable range
Send the stabilized water to filtration and record gas feed rate, pH, and alkalinity

tasks.explanation: Recarbonation lowers pH in controlled stages with measurement between stages, so the water reaches the filters stable and does not deposit scale or turn corrosive.

tasks.prompt: Order the softening sludge handling sequence for a solids contact clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening plant in western Canada managing lime sludge from clarifier to lagoon.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blanket monitoring through sludge placed in the lagoon cell.

cards.label: Measure the sludge blanket depth and the solids content of a blanket sample
Set the sludge withdrawal rate to hold the blanket inside its target depth band
Withdraw sludge to the thickening or holding tank and confirm transfer by tank level rise
Dewater or condition the sludge as the site program directs and check the liquid return quality
Place the sludge in the assigned lagoon cell and record the cell, volume, and date
Review lagoon capacity against the seasonal plan and report the remaining room to the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: Sludge handling is paced by blanket measurement, verified by holding tank level, and closed by lagoon accounting so softening capacity is never lost to an unmanaged blanket or a full lagoon.

tasks.prompt: Order the calibration program for lime and soda ash feeders.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 operator in Manitoba calibrating dry chemical feeders on a softening plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: feeder shutdown checks through calibrated feeders returned to service.

cards.label: Take one feeder out of service at a time so softening continues on the remaining equipment
Clean the feeder, hopper outlet, and dissolving or slaking chamber and inspect for bridging and wear
Run the feeder at several set points and collect and weigh the output over a timed interval at each setting
Plot delivered rate against set point and adjust the feeder control to correct any offset
Return the feeder to service and confirm softened hardness and pH hold at the calibrated rate
Record the calibration curve and date in the chemical program file for both feeders

tasks.explanation: Dry feeder calibration weighs timed output at several set points, corrects the control from the plotted curve, and proves the correction in softened water quality before the record is filed.

tasks.prompt: Order the hardness monitoring program across a softening plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening system in Saskatchewan with raw, clarifier effluent, filtered, and finished sampling points.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program sampling round through the trended hardness review.

cards.label: Collect samples at raw, clarifier effluent, filtered, and finished points at the program times
Measure total hardness and calcium hardness on each sample and pH and alkalinity on the treated samples
Calculate magnesium hardness and stage removals and compare each stage with its control band
Investigate any stage outside its band by checking the related feeder delivery and blanket depth first
Plot the day results on the hardness trend chart and note any dose or feeder change made
Review the weekly trend with the operator in charge and set any dose table revision

tasks.explanation: Stage by stage hardness monitoring locates a softening problem to one unit, and the feeder and blanket checks come before any dose change is considered.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to rising finished hardness during a softening run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening plant in western Canada where finished hardness climbed steadily over two days.
tasks.configuration: Scope: confirmed hardness rise through hardness restored and cause recorded.

cards.label: Confirm the rise with a fresh finished sample and check the bench hardness result against the online reading if fitted
Sample clarifier effluent hardness to learn whether breakthrough starts at the clarifier or later
Check lime and soda ash feeder deliveries by timed output and day tank or hopper levels
Check sludge blanket depth and withdrawal, since a high blanket carries precipitate into the effluent
Correct the cause found, then hold or reduce flow if hardness is still rising toward the plant limit
Monitor hardness hourly until two consecutive results are back in band and record the cause and fix

tasks.explanation: The response works from finished water back to the clarifier, then to feeders and blanket, correcting the first proven cause instead of raising both chemical doses at once.

tasks.prompt: Order a cold weather softening operating program for slow reaction water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional softening plant in northern Alberta facing very cold raw water and slower precipitation reactions.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal program set up through winter operating checks.

cards.label: Measure raw temperature and hardness and note the longer reaction time needed at the cold condition
Increase contact time by lowering clarifier loading or bringing the standby contact unit into service
Confirm lime slaking quality, since poor slaking in cold conditions cuts effective dose
Raise sludge blanket inventory within its band to seed precipitation in the slow reacting water
Increase hardness sampling frequency and judge doses only after the longer reaction time has passed
Record the winter dose and loading settings in the seasonal program for the next cold period

tasks.explanation: Cold water slows softening reactions, so the winter program buys contact time and blanket seeding first and judges dose changes only after the longer reaction has had time to complete.

tasks.prompt: Order the shutdown and cleaning sequence for a solids contact clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional annual cleaning of a solids contact softening clarifier in western Canada.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clarifier in service through the cleaned unit ready to refill.

cards.label: Shift softening production to the remaining unit or storage and confirm finished water supply is protected
Stop raw flow and chemical feeds to the unit and let the blanket settle
Drain the unit to the sludge system and remove accumulated scale and sludge deposits
Wash down reaction and settling zones and inspect drives, scrapers, and sample lines while the unit is empty
Repair or clear defects found and record the inspection in the asset file
Close drains, refill slowly, and hold the unit ready for a controlled return to service

tasks.explanation: Cleaning protects supply first, drains sludge in a controlled way to the sludge system, and uses the empty unit for inspection before a slow refill prepares it for service.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of an oxidation and filtration plant for iron and manganese.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional groundwater plant in Manitoba with aeration, chemical oxidation, detention, and pressure filters.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wells at rest through treated water meeting iron and manganese targets.

cards.label: Analyse raw well water for iron, manganese, pH, alkalinity, and dissolved oxygen
Start aeration and confirm air flow and water distribution over the aerator are even
Start the oxidant feed at the dose set for the measured iron and manganese and confirm delivery by drawdown
Fill the detention tank and allow the full oxidation contact time before filtration
Start filtration at a reduced rate and sample filtered iron and manganese
Raise flow to normal only when filtered results meet targets and record doses and results

tasks.explanation: Iron and manganese must be fully oxidized during detention before filtration, so flow is raised only after filtered samples prove the oxidation step worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the potassium permanganate feed program for manganese control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan using potassium permanganate ahead of greensand style filters for manganese removal.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program set up through steady manganese removal without permanganate carryover.

cards.label: Measure raw manganese, iron, pH, and oxidant demand on a fresh well sample
Run bench oxidant demand tests to set the starting permanganate dose for the raw water
Prepare the solution at the program strength and calibrate the feed pump by drawdown
Feed permanganate ahead of the contact tank and confirm a faint residual reaches the filter influent without pink water past the filters
Sample filtered manganese and check for any pink colour in filtered water at each check round
Trim the dose in small steps to the lowest dose that holds filtered manganese on target and record the program dose

tasks.explanation: The permanganate program is set by bench demand, proven by drawdown, and trimmed to the lowest dose that removes manganese without carrying pink water through the filters.

tasks.prompt: Order the chlorine oxidation program for iron removal on a well supply.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional well supply in Alberta using free chlorine as the oxidant ahead of dual media pressure filters.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dose setting through a stable iron removal operation.

cards.label: Measure raw iron, manganese, pH, ammonia, and chlorine demand, since demand consumes oxidant first
Set the chlorine dose to satisfy demand and still hold the oxidant residual set for iron oxidation at the filter influent
Feed chlorine at the well discharge ahead of the contact tank and confirm delivery by drawdown
Hold the full contact time and observe oxidized iron formation in a contact tank sample
Filter at the program rate and sample filtered iron, manganese, and free chlorine residual
Adjust dose only from filtered results and contact tank residual together and log the operating dose

tasks.explanation: Chlorine must satisfy raw demand before it can oxidize iron, so the dose is judged by the contact tank residual and filtered iron together, never by dose alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the regeneration sequence for a catalytic manganese greensand filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional batch greensand filter in western Canada due for regeneration after a long manganese run.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter removed from service through the regenerated filter back in production.

cards.label: Take the filter out of service and backwash it to remove accumulated solids and loosen the bed
Drain the filter to the regeneration level specified for the vessel
Introduce the permanganate regeneration solution and hold the soak for the full program contact time
Rinse the filter slowly until the rinse water runs clear with no pink colour remaining
Return the filter to service at a reduced rate and run filter to waste while manganese removal recovers
Confirm filtered manganese meets target before placing the filter in full production and record the regeneration

tasks.explanation: Regeneration restores the catalytic coating in order: clean the bed, soak at the correct level and time, rinse until no permanganate remains, and prove removal before full production.

tasks.prompt: Order a sequestration program for a small well system with low iron and manganese.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small community well system in British Columbia with low iron and manganese below the level that justifies filtration.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program approval checks through steady sequestered supply.

cards.label: Confirm by sampling that iron and manganese levels and water chemistry suit sequestration for this system
Select the sequestering product and set the dose from the measured iron and manganese and the supplier program factors
Feed the product at the well discharge so it mixes before any aeration or chlorine contact that would oxidize the metals
Confirm feed delivery by drawdown and check that no staining complaints or deposits appear at system sample points
Sample distribution iron, manganese, and chlorine residual on the program schedule
Review staining reports and sample results each season and reassess whether filtration is now needed

tasks.explanation: Sequestration keeps metals dissolved and colourless only if the product is fed before oxidation points, so feed location, delivery proof, and distribution sampling carry the program.

tasks.prompt: Order the iron and manganese sampling program for a multi well field.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional well field in western Canada with four wells of differing iron and manganese content.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sampling round planning through well specific treatment settings updated.

cards.label: List each well and its sample points: raw wellhead, blended plant influent, and filtered water
Collect raw samples well by well and measure iron, manganese, pH, and alkalinity for each well
Calculate the blended influent metals load from the wells in service and their flows
Compare filtered results with targets and relate any rise to the well combination in service
Update the oxidant dose for the current well blend and record the dose basis in the log
File well by well trends and flag any well with rising metals for investigation

tasks.explanation: Well specific sampling separates the contribution of each well, so oxidant dose follows the actual blend in service rather than an average that fits no blend.

tasks.prompt: Order the aeration and detention oxidation sequence for a high iron well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional high iron well plant in Manitoba using cascade aeration and a detention tank ahead of filtration.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw well water through oxidized water entering the filters.

cards.label: Start the well pump and set aerator water distribution so flow spreads evenly over the trays
Confirm aeration raises dissolved oxygen and strips carbon dioxide, checking raw and aerated pH
Add chemical oxidant after aeration where the program requires it for the remaining iron load
Pass the water through the detention tank for the full oxidation time at the current flow
Check a detention outlet sample for complete iron oxidation before filtration
Send the oxidized water to the filters and record aerator condition, dose, and detention results

tasks.explanation: Aeration does the first oxidation work and raises pH, chemical oxidant finishes the load, and detention time is proven by an outlet sample before the filters receive the water.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter ripening program after backwashing an iron and manganese filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional pressure filter plant in Saskatchewan where manganese removal dips after every backwash.
tasks.configuration: Scope: end of backwash through full manganese removal restored.

cards.label: Backwash at the program rate and duration so the catalytic media surface is cleaned but not stripped
Return the filter at a reduced filtration rate with oxidant feed confirmed at the influent
Run filter to waste or recycle while filtered manganese is sampled at set intervals
Watch filtered manganese fall as the catalytic surface reconditions and note the ripening time
Place the filter in full production only when filtered manganese meets target on two consecutive samples
Record ripening time in the filter log and use it to set the plant ripening allowance

tasks.explanation: Manganese filters remove best on a conditioned catalytic surface, so ripening is measured by repeated filtered samples and the filter returns to production only on proven results.

tasks.prompt: Order the backwash program review for iron and manganese pressure filters.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 operator in Alberta reviewing backwash practice on iron removal pressure filters.
tasks.configuration: Scope: run data review through revised backwash settings in service.

cards.label: Gather filter run lengths, headloss trends, and filtered iron results for the review period
Observe a full backwash and measure wash rate, duration, and waste water appearance through the wash
Check media condition and depth at the inspection port for fouling, loss, or cemented deposits
Adjust wash rate or duration in one change only where the evidence shows under or over washing
Run the revised wash on the next cycle and compare headloss recovery and filtered iron with the baseline
Record the revised settings and the evidence for the change in the filter program file

tasks.explanation: The review changes one wash variable at a time from observed evidence, then proves the new setting by headloss recovery and filtered quality on the next cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to black water complaints linked to manganese release.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional community in western Canada reporting black water after a distribution flow reversal stirred manganese deposits.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first complaints through plant and system manganese control restored.

cards.label: Collect complaint locations and times and sample chlorine residual, iron, and manganese at affected points
Check plant filtered manganese and recent oxidant dose records to rule out a treatment breakthrough
Inspect for a flow reversal, main break, or hydrant use that disturbed distribution deposits
Flush affected mains in a planned sequence from clean areas toward the affected area
Confirm manganese and colour at flushed points have returned to normal before closing the event
Record the event, review plant manganese trending, and set added distribution manganese sampling for the following week

tasks.explanation: Black water response first separates a plant breakthrough from a distribution deposit release, then flushes in a planned direction and closes only on normal samples.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily CT verification program for a baffled clearwell.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada disinfecting with free chlorine through a baffled clearwell under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: morning operating data through the filed daily CT result.

cards.label: Record the lowest clearwell level for the period and the contact volume at that level
Record the highest flow rate through the clearwell for the same period
Calculate theoretical detention time from contact volume divided by peak flow
Apply the clearwell baffling factor to obtain the effective contact time
Measure free chlorine residual, temperature, and pH at the clearwell outlet
Calculate CT from residual and effective time, compare with the required CT for the conditions, and file the result

tasks.explanation: Daily CT uses worst case pairing: lowest volume, highest flow, and the baffling factor all come before the measured residual is applied, so the filed value is the conservative one.

tasks.prompt: Order the CT management program for very cold treated water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in northern Saskatchewan where winter water near freezing raises the CT required for the same inactivation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal CT review through winter CT settings in service.

cards.label: Measure treated water temperature and confirm the required CT for the cold condition from the plant CT tables
Review clearwell level control and raise the minimum operating level to gain contact volume if needed
Check the baffling factor in use still matches the clearwell configuration at the winter level
Set the winter chlorine dose so the outlet residual delivers the required CT at peak winter flow
Verify the calculated winter CT daily for the first week and trend residual and temperature together
Record the winter CT settings in the seasonal program and set the spring review date

tasks.explanation: Cold water raises required CT, so the winter program gains time through level control first, then sets residual to meet the higher requirement, and proves it with a week of daily checks.

tasks.prompt: Order a breakpoint chlorination study for an ammonia bearing well water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional groundwater plant in Manitoba with natural ammonia that consumes chlorine before a free residual forms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bench breakpoint curve through the adopted plant dose.

cards.label: Measure raw ammonia, chlorine demand, pH, and alkalinity on a fresh sample
Dose a bench series with increasing chlorine and hold each sample for the standard contact time
Measure free and total chlorine in each sample and plot residual against dose to locate the breakpoint
Select the operating dose past the breakpoint that holds the target free residual with a safety margin
Trial the dose at plant scale and confirm free residual at the contactor outlet and in distribution samples
Record the breakpoint dose basis and the ammonia conditions in the disinfection program file

tasks.explanation: The breakpoint is found from a plotted bench curve, not guessed, and the plant dose is set past the breakpoint so a true free residual survives into distribution.

tasks.prompt: Order the conversion of a small plant from free chlorine to chloramine awareness program steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small plant in western Canada planning a chloramine conversion study with provincial drinking water requirements considered in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: feasibility review through the decision record, with conversion only if every gate passes.

cards.label: Review distribution water age, residual history, and byproduct results to confirm a reason to study chloramine
Measure source ammonia background and assess nitrification risk points in storage and dead ends
Bench test chlorine and ammonia ratios and confirm the combined residual forms and holds as expected
Set a nitrification monitoring plan covering storage, dead ends, and warm locations before any conversion
Prepare customer and health unit notification material as the provincial program requires in general terms
Record the go or no go decision with its evidence and file the monitoring plan with the decision

tasks.explanation: A chloramine decision weighs nitrification risk and monitoring readiness alongside residual stability, so the monitoring plan exists before any conversion could proceed.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal disinfection strategy review for a reservoir source plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia reviewing disinfection before the warm algae and high demand season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: past season data review through the adopted warm season strategy.

cards.label: Review last warm season residuals, byproduct results, taste and odour events, and CT records
Measure current raw organics, temperature, and chlorine demand to set the season starting point
Confirm pretreatment and enhanced coagulation settings that lower demand before disinfection
Set the warm season dose, residual targets, and CT checks for plant and distribution control points
Schedule added byproduct and residual sampling for the high demand period
Brief all shifts on the strategy and file it as the seasonal disinfection plan

tasks.explanation: The seasonal strategy lowers demand through pretreatment first, then sets dose and residual targets, so disinfection is not asked to compensate for untreated organics load.

tasks.prompt: Order a clearwell tracer study to confirm the baffling factor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Alberta verifying the baffling factor used in its CT calculations.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study planning through the adopted baffling factor.

cards.label: Choose a tracer and dose that can be measured accurately at the clearwell outlet and set the study flow
Hold clearwell level and flow steady for the study period and record both continuously
Introduce the tracer as a step or pulse at the clearwell inlet at the recorded start time
Sample the outlet at short intervals and plot outlet tracer concentration against time
Determine the time for the leading tracer fraction to appear and calculate the baffling factor from the detention time
Adopt the studied factor in CT calculations, file the study, and note the configuration it applies to

tasks.explanation: A tracer study measures real short circuiting at steady level and flow, and the adopted factor is tied to the configuration studied so later changes trigger a restudy.

tasks.prompt: Order a chlorine residual decay study in treated water storage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional system in western Canada with a ground reservoir where residuals fall between plant and far end samples.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study set up through residual control actions adopted.

cards.label: Select study points at the plant outlet, reservoir inlet and outlet, and two distribution locations
Sample free chlorine, temperature, and pH at every point at the same rounds for several days
Calculate water age indicators from reservoir levels and flows for the study period
Plot residual loss against storage time and identify where the largest decay occurs
Set actions such as reservoir turnover, mixing, or dose adjustment matched to the location of the loss
Repeat one sampling round after the actions and confirm residual recovery before closing the study

tasks.explanation: The decay study pairs every residual with its location and storage time, so corrective action is aimed at the storage step where chlorine is actually lost.

tasks.prompt: Order the disinfection byproduct monitoring program for a surface water plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional surface water plant in western Canada monitoring disinfection byproducts under the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program design through the annual results review.

cards.label: Select sample locations that represent the oldest water and highest formation potential in the system
Set the sampling schedule to cover warm water and high organics periods when formation is highest
Collect samples with the required preservative and quenching, and complete chain of custody records
Record plant dose, treated organics, temperature, and pH for each sampling round
Compare results with the guideline values and with the plant action levels and trend them by season
Where results trend upward, assign pretreatment or dose strategy actions and review them at the annual program review

tasks.explanation: Byproduct sampling targets oldest water in the highest formation season, and every result is read with the dose and organics data that explain it.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet disinfection operating program for a plant with chlorine residual.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia using ultraviolet disinfection for primary inactivation and chlorine for the distribution residual.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily UV checks through monthly performance review.

cards.label: Confirm filtered water turbidity and ultraviolet transmittance are inside the validated UV operating range
Check lamp status, intensity readings, and sleeve cleaning system operation at start up
Set flow through the reactor within the validated range and confirm the calculated dose meets the target
Add chlorine after the reactor and confirm the distribution residual at the plant outlet
Record intensity, transmittance, flow, and dose each shift and alarm any out of range condition
Review dose compliance and lamp hours monthly and schedule lamp or sleeve work from the trend

tasks.explanation: UV dose depends on transmittance, intensity, and flow together, so all three are checked before flow is set, and chlorine still follows the reactor for the distribution residual.
